taxonomy_assessment: The F1..F4 taxonomy held up well and cleanly absorbed 40 of 41 photos (one blank image → OTHER). Every physical product mapped to exactly one family with no forced fits, and the four families are genuinely distinct on the axis that matters commercially: F1_floral = non-edible silk/real-touch arrangements (dominant, ~49% of products); F4_mixed_hamper = multi-item themed gift boxes containing chocolate/candy plus toys/balloons/props (~30%); F3_candy_basket = edible-candy-forward baskets/bouquets where sweets ARE the display (~11%); F2_framed = wall-mount shadow-box floral frames (a small but structurally unique form, ~5%). The edible/perishable flags cut across families usefully and should be treated as independent facets, not folded into family. Grouping reduced 40 product photos to 36 distinct products via four confident multi-shot merges (4054/4058, 4066/4067, 4084/4095/4096, 4109/4113). I deliberately kept several conservative splits: the handbag-basket 'sisters' IMG_3203 vs IMG_3358 (different accents: turquoise bow vs blue-pearl hoop) and the two shadow-box frames IMG_3116 vs IMG_3117 (different palettes) are near-identical forms but not provably the same SKU, so they remain separate. Net: the taxonomy is sound for launch; the main strain is that F1 is doing a lot of work and would benefit from sub-tagging rather than new top-level families.
taxonomy_adjustments: Keep F1..F4 as the top-level families - no new top-level family is warranted by this sample.

Add facet tags WITHIN F1_floral rather than splitting it, since it holds ~50% of products. Suggested sub-tags: 'box-arrangement' (cube/cylinder/fabric box: 3106, 3140, 3371, 3389, 3476, 4066/4067), 'basket-arrangement' (wicker handle basket: 3127), 'handbag-basket' (grey woven purse baskets with hoop handle: 3203, 3358, 3373, 3378), 'tray-hoop' (3500), 'gift-bag-posy' (2770).
Treat 'handbag-basket / purse-basket floral' as a recognised sub-cluster of F1 (4 products: 3203, 3358, 3373, 3378) - it is a repeated distinctive form and a likely merchandising collection.

Consider whether F2_framed (only 2 products) stays its own family or becomes an F1 sub-tag 'framed/wall-decor'. Recommend keeping F2 separate because the wall-mount glass shadow-box is a fundamentally different product use (home decor vs gift bouquet).

The F3 vs F4 boundary needs an explicit rule: F3 = display is candy/marshmallow itself (2812, 3254, 3403, 3136); F4 = box contains packaged chocolate/candy plus non-food items (teddy, balloon, tumbler, wine). IMG_3136 was borderline (candy + teddy + flowers) and placed in F3 because candy dominates the visible display - flag for owner review.

Add an independent 'baby/gender' facet, not a family. A strong blue-boy vs pink-girl vs neutral cluster spans F1, F3 and F4 (2718, 3136, 3386, 3389, 4054/4058, 4109/4113 = boy; 3399, 3403 = girl) and is more useful as a filter than as a family.
Add an 'alcohol' flag: IMG_3153 and IMG_3591 contain sparkling wine, which has shipping/age-restriction implications distinct from the generic perishable flag.
